To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the D416A mutation does not affect the active-centre conformation of the H. insolens Cel6A, and that the active-centre loop adopts a more open conformed in the D416A Cel6A than in the wild-type enzyme.
the active-site structure of a GH-6 enzyme is similar to the T. reesei enzyme and that the N-terminal loop of H. insolens Cel6 is in a more open position.

the D416A mutation in the active centre loop of the H.insolens cellobiohydrolyase Cel6A does not affect the substrate distortion at the -1 subsites and that the active centre loop is more open than in the T. reesei Cel7A and T. reese (1999), Biochemistry, 38, 14125-14131] Cel6A structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of action and the substrate specificity of glycoside hyd rolasses.
the structure and function of the cellulolytic enzymes of family GH-6.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of cellulases and the role of the Brønsted acid/base in the enzymatic degradation of the cellulose chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the role of Asp416 is still unclear, the active-centre loop of the H.insolens Cel6A enzyme is flexible and that the loop conformation is not dependent upon the presence of substrate in the active centre.
, in the H. insol ens Cel6A D415A mutant in complex at the -1 subsites, substrate distortion is observed and the catalytic N-terminal loop adopts a more open con formation.

the role of the putative general acid/base residue Asp416 in H. insolens Cel6B is to facilitate the distortion of the glycosidic linkage of the -1 substrate subsite, rather than to act as the general base in catalysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the active-centre loop of H. insolens Cel6 is not a key determinant of substrate binding or distortion, and is not required for catalysis.
the role of a potential BrØnsted base in the active site is not essential for catalysis, and that the N-terminal loop flexibility is not a prerequisite for catalysis.
a single residue in the active-centre region of a family 6 cellobiohyrolase can be mutated to alanine without affecting the catalytic efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a potential catalytic base residue is not required for catalytic activity, but the presence of the loop in an extended conformation is required for efficient hydrolysis.
the catalytic aspartate is not essential for substrate distortion.

the D416A mutation does not affect the ability of the enzyme to distort substrate in the -1 and -1+1 subsites, and the active-centre loop remains flexible, but the enzyme is unable to bind substrate in a productive orientation and thus the mutant is inactive.
